summary: Watson Butte L-4 ground cab in the Umpqua National Forest, Oregon; collapsed in winter 2021-22, and a July 2022 visit found only a pile of boards.

facts.status_note: Collapsed in the winter of 2021-22; a July 2022 visit found only a pile of boards

access.note: A notice on the 2022 trip report says the area was closed as of July 20, 2024 because of the active Diamond Complex; no later status was found

visit.trail_note: Nothing stands to climb. The 2022 trip report describes Watson Butte Trail #1443 as about 1.1 miles from the trailhead to the summit, reached over poorly marked roads

events.note: A telephone line was extended to the summit before the lookout was built

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates a rag camp to 1934 and the L-4 cab to 1937. The Roaming Civic says the Forest Service notes 1934 but other sources say 1937, and the Forest Lookouts page gives 1933 for a lookout. The story reports these dates without choosing one.
The Roaming Civic says snow most likely caused the collapse, while the Forest Lookouts page gives only weather-related causes. Both point to the 2021-22 winter.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checks out: coordinates, 1,733 m elevation, L-4 design, Douglas County, and the April 22, 2011 FFLOS registration all match the register. The build date conflicts (1933, 1934, 1937) are reported, not resolved. Staffing is thin: a 1962 newspaper item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page and the Roaming Civic line that it was not actively staffed after the 1960s. The access level closed comes from a July 2024 notice on a 2022 page and may be out of date; a search turned up closure news for the Umpqua but no newer notice for this site, and none was read. The Forest Lookouts page also quotes a 1942 Umpqua archive photo caption, but it has no URL, so it is not listed as a photo. The firelookout.com page was read but is not cited because it adds nothing new.
